decisions.thought: Plan: Lead Incineroar for Intimidate and Fake Out, with Parting Shot for pivoting. Garchomp (Mega) is my main damage dealer and hits Gholdengo and Kingambit hard. Kingambit handles Dragonite and Mimikyu. Watch for Rotom-Wash and Dragonite Multiscale/Inner Focus, and Garchomp's ground moves against Gholdengo. Opponent Garchomp may have Rough Skin.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Looking at the opponent's roster against my team, I'm leaning toward Incineroar for its intimidate and utility moves, alongside Garchomp and Corviknight for their strength and coverage against most of their threats.

Actually, Kingambit's Supreme Overlord ability gives it strong offensive pressure and fine matchups against their fairy and dark-type threats. I'll settle on Incineroar, Garchomp, and Kingambit, leading with Incineroar.

decisions.thought: Plan: Rotom leads vs Incin/Chomp/Corv with Hydro/Wisp/Volt. Gholdengo Nasty Plot sweeps Sinistcha, immune FakeOut/Parting. Scarf Chomp cleans all: EQ for Incin/King/Ghold, Poison Sinistcha, Stone Corv, Dragon Chomp. Avoid Gholdengo into Kingambit.

decisions.thought: Opponent team: Gholdengo, Kingambit, Dragonite, Rotom-Wash, Garchomp, Mimikyu. Rotom-Wash (Levitate, immune to Earthquake) is in front and already at -1 Atk from Intimidate. Turn 1: Fake Out for chip and flinch. Then Flare Blitz or Parting Shot to pivot. Garchomp (Mega) is my main damage, so bring it in against Gholdengo or Kingambit. Watch for Rough Skin, which can hurt my Garchomp when it makes contact.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Incineroar is already down a stage from Intimidate against Rotom-Wash. Since it's turn one, Fake Out is available and hits for solid damage with a guaranteed flinch, and since it's Normal-type it works fine against the Electric/Water Rotom-Wash despite its Levitate ability. That seems like the right opening move.

decisions.thought: Plan: Rotom vs Incin, Gholdengo vs Sinistcha immune FakeOut/Parting, Scarf Chomp cleans. Avoid Gholdengo into Kingambit. T1 Protect scouts likely Fake Out, then Hydro/Wisp/Volt pivot.

decisions.thought: Opponent: Rotom-Wash (Levitate, immune to Earthquake, has Protect, now at -1 Atk). Its other members are still hidden: Gholdengo, Kingambit, Dragonite, Garchomp, Mimikyu. Flare Blitz is resisted by Rotom-Wash, so I'll use Parting Shot to weaken it further and pivot. Kingambit resists Electric and takes Water neutrally, so it is a good switch-in for Rotom-Wash. Garchomp should come in for Gholdengo or Kingambit. Watch for Rough Skin on Garchomp's contact moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Facing Incineroar against Rotom-Wash, I'm weighing options since Flare Blitz won't do much against its Water typing and Garchomp's Earthquake is useless against Levitate — Parting Shot to debuff Rotom and pivot to Garchomp or Kingambit seems like the better line.

Kingambit actually makes a solid switch-in here: as Dark/Steel it resists the Electric STAB and takes Water neutrally, so it can tank a hit and threaten back with Sucker Punch or Kowtow Cleave. I'm now considering whether a second Parting Shot to stack another -1 Atk/SpA before bringing Kingambit in is worth the tempo loss.

decisions.thought: Incineroar used Parting Shot and must switch out. Rotom-Wash is at -2 Atk and -1 SpA, and it has Protect and Will-O-Wisp. Garchomp is immune to its Electric moves, outspeeds it, and can Mega Evolve. Earthquake will not hit Rotom-Wash because of Levitate, so use Dragon Claw or Stone Edge. Kingambit is the other option, but Garchomp is the stronger pick here. Watch for Will-O-Wisp on Garchomp.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since Parting Shot forces a switch, Incineroar must leave the field and only a switch is legal — I'll bring in Garchomp.

Comparing options against Rotom-Wash: Garchomp is immune to Electric via its Ground typing and outspeeds Rotom-Wash, while Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing doesn't give it clean resistances against Rotom's dual attacking types. Garchomp seems like the safer switch-in here.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp is now active against Rotom-Wash, which is at -2 Atk and can't be hit by Earthquake because of Levitate. Dragon Claw is 100% accurate and neutral, so I'm using it to pressure Rotom-Wash. Watch for Will-O-Wisp on Garchomp; if it lands, switch to Kingambit or Incineroar. Gholdengo, Dragonite and Mimikyu are still unseen. Kingambit handles Dragonite and Mimikyu, and Garchomp is the main answer to Gholdengo.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp is Dragon/Ground, so Thunderbolt from Rotom-Wash has no effect on it; only Hydro Pump matters there.

Rotom-Wash resists nothing from Garchomp's physical options, so both Dragon Claw and Stone Edge hit neutrally, though Rotom-Wash's solid defense limits damage. With Rotom-Wash's Attack lowered, it's less threatening physically, though Will-O-Wisp could still come out to cripple Garchomp. I'm leaning toward Stone Edge as the attack choice.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Garchomp is burned at 112/185 HP, facing a Rotom-Wash at 64% with -2 Attack. Earthquake won't work since Rotom-Wash has Levitate and is immune to Ground moves, so I should avoid it and use Dragon Claw instead since Garchomp outspeeds.

Dragon Claw already did around 20% last time and has perfect accuracy, which beats Stone Edge's 80% accuracy option since Rock type isn't super effective against Rotom's Electric/Water typing anyway. I'll go with Dragon Claw.

Rotom has Protect, Will-O-Wisp and Hydro Pump, which took about 48 HP from Garchomp last time, so Garchomp is near its limit. Gholdengo, Dragonite, Mimikyu, Garchomp and Kingambit are still unseen. decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp is burned at 53/185, and Rotom-Wash is at 43% with -2 Attack and Levitate, so Earthquake won't work despite being listed as super effective. Stone Edge would be neutral against its Electric/Water typing, so I'm leaning toward Dragon Claw instead.

Dragon Claw previously did about 21% to Rotom, so I'd need two more hits to finish it off, but Rotom's Hydro Pump already dealt 48 damage last time and could nearly knock out Garchomp's remaining 53 HP. Stone Edge's crit chance makes it slightly stronger on average but with lower accuracy, so Dragon Claw is the safer choice even though Garchomp risks going down to a follow-up Hydro Pump.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Rotom-Wash is at 24% HP but faster than Incineroar, with Hydro Pump resisted by Incineroar's Fire typing and Rotom's SpA dropped a stage. I'm weighing whether Incineroar could use Fake Out, but that's only viable on its first turn in, so it's not an option here.

If I switch Kingambit in, it takes neutral Hydro Pump damage but is slower, so Rotom would attack first before Kingambit's Sucker Punch. The bigger threat is Flare Blitz from Incineroar, which could knock out Rotom despite Water resisting Fire given Rotom's low remaining HP.

Also Will-O-Wisp is irrelevant since Incineroar is immune to burn as Fire type. Flare Blitz is the clear choice here.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm assessing the matchup: Garchomp outspeeds our Incineroar at 148/202 HP and could threaten with Earthquake, Dragon Claw, or Stone Edge, and there's a chance it mega evolves next turn since it hasn't yet.

Flare Blitz from Incineroar isn't very effective against Garchomp's Dragon typing, so that's a weak option. Switching to Kingambit looks better since its Dark/Steel typing resists Dragon moves, though it's still vulnerable to Earthquake.

Parting Shot could work well too — it drops Garchomp's Atk/SpA by one stage while bringing in Kingambit safely, though Kingambit would still need to tank an Earthquake on the switch-in, which could deal significant damage given the type disadvantage.

Opponent Garchomp (100%, not yet Mega, item unknown) is faster and likely to Earthquake, which is super effective on Kingambit. Kingambit should survive one Earthquake, so I'm attacking with Kowtow Cleave for the most damage. decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit's at 207 HP with 205 Attack, now boosted by Supreme Overlord at 1.2x since two allies (Garchomp and Incineroar) have fainted. I'm checking whether the opposing Garchomp could still Mega Evolve this turn since it hasn't yet.

Garchomp outspeeds Kingambit and will likely lead with Earthquake, which hits for super effective damage against Kingambit's Steel typing. But if Garchomp attacks, Sucker Punch becomes viable and lets Kingambit strike first — with Black Glasses and Supreme Overlord boosts, Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave both hit roughly similarly hard. The key question is whether Kingambit's 207 HP and boosted Defense can survive an incoming Earthquake, especially factoring in whether Garchomp's Attack was already lowered by an earlier Parting Shot.

Comparing the two options, Sucker Punch gives less raw damage despite its speed priority, while Kowtow Cleave likely deals more damage and Kingambit probably survives the incoming Earthquake anyway. I'll go with Kowtow Cleave as the better choice.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Kingambit is at 24/207 HP against Garchomp at roughly 24% health, and I'm factoring in Rough Skin recoil plus Supreme Overlord's boost from two fainted allies. Since Garchomp outspeeds, it'll attack first this turn, so I need to think through what happens if it goes first.

If Garchomp uses Earthquake, that's super effective against Kingambit's Steel typing and will knock it out outright given the low HP, regardless of my earlier assumption it could survive one hit. That means my only real path is Sucker Punch, since it has priority and could take Garchomp down before it acts—I'm now calculating whether Kingambit's boosted attack stat is enough to finish off Garchomp's remaining HP with that move.
